clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory instruction task for proficient skinners traveling through Elwynn Forest. It directs adventurers to Helene Peltskinner in Goldshire to learn how to fashion a Camp Chair out of harvested hides. Learning to craft personal camp furnishings allows wilderness travelers to rest and recuperate far beyond the safety of settled towns.

For wilderness hunters and scouts, the art of harvesting beast hides provides more than trade goods and armor scraps. Seasoned skinners can fashion field amenities like a Camp Chair, allowing travelers to sit, rest their limbs, and maintain peak physical condition during long treks through dangerous lands. Helene Peltskinner in Goldshire instructs proficient skinners on how to turn raw beast pelts into comfortable campsite seating.

Setting up a field rest requires respect for local settlements and proper outdoor preparation. Most townspeople frown upon adventurers pitching personal camps in the town square, requiring travelers to head into the wilderness before unrolling their gear. Furthermore, no field site is truly viable without a campfire, leading many skinners to study basic culinary arts to master fire-building.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Being able to skillfully harvest the skins and hides of fallen beasts is one of the more valuable skills an adventurer can possess.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Camp Chair for your camp. Sometimes it's important to just take a load off, and you can use some of those hides you've gathered to make a comfy chair to sit in. A bit of relaxation can help ensure that you are at your peak condition and can strike where it counts the next time you find yourself in a dust-up.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Camp Chair. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
